title: Engineers' Café All-Hands — Apr 28 2027
content:
Engineers' Café — Org sync notes (informal)/Apr 28 2027

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (host)
- Marco Hernandez
- Lina Chen
- Owen Park
- ~36 engineers joined live, ~12 watched recording

Agenda:
1) Quick wins + metrics (5m)
2) Project spotlights: KV-cache rollup, quantization canary, Dedicated autoscale tuning (20m)
3) Postmortem summary: INC-2027-134 (10m)
4) Community lightning: RFC preview, infra debt list (5m)
5) Q&A + parking lot (10m)

TL;DR highlights:
- Observed 18% tail-latency reduction after rolling the KV-cache LRU eviction fix to canary tenants (metrics look stable).
- Quantization v2 builds on-nightly are functionally equivalent in 95% of eval prompts; edge hallucination profile increased slightly on long-code tasks (tracked).
- Dedicated autoscaling: improved throughput by 1.3x for bursty request patterns after switching to the new burst policy; some teams reported higher preheat costs — follow-up required.
- Incident INC-2027-134 (OOM cascade in multi-tenant staging) root cause: stale KV cache entries + unexpected sequence length spike; mitigations: smaller cache shard size + per-tenant sequence caps.

1) Quick wins and metrics:
- Lina: rolling 2.1.3 of kv-cache to 10% of hosted traffic. Early telemetry: mean token latency -7%, p99 -18% on short-inference paths. CPU usage on CPU-backed embedder nodes unchanged.
- Owen: added a lightweight tracer tag to requests to surface batch composition in Console (linked in artifacts). Will iterate on UI follow-up.

2) Project spotlights
- KV-cache optimization (Lina)
  - What: LRU eviction heuristics + shard compacting to avoid stale pointers after model swap.
  - Outcome: reduction in redundant KV lookups; memory churn down ~22% on canary clusters.
  - Open: edge case when model variant switch happens mid-session; PR #7889 is in review (Marco).
  - Note: add a small cross-check in release job to validate cache consistency after model swap.

- Quantization canary (Marco)
  - Status: nightly build of quantize-v2 deployed to dedicated-canary-3. Ran eval suite on prompts-2027q1.
  - Observations: accuracy parity on summarization; small regression on long code-generation (>1024 tokens) where tokenization boundary interacts with per-head scale.
  - Action: Lina to run focused eval set for code tasks and propose fallback threshold for live routing.

- Dedicated autoscale tuning (Owen)
  - Changed burst-policy to pre-warm nodes for sudden spikes; increased pre-warm threshold from 60s to 20s.
  - Result: sustained throughput improvement for short spikes; cost delta visible in daily reports (approx +6% for affected pools).
  - Decision: keep policy but add an option to limit pre-warm for non-critical tenants.

3) Postmortem summary: INC-2027-134 (OOM cascade)
- Timeline (short): staging cluster hit a sequence length storm caused by a misrouted ingestion job; stale KV pointers triggered memory leak in a hot path; cascade to other tenants due to shared allocator settings.
- Root cause: combination of (a) ingestion job misconfiguration, (b) cache shard compaction not triggered for long-running sessions, (c) shared allocator thresholds that were too permissive.
- Immediate fixes applied: reverted last-week allocator tweak, forced cache compaction job, added sequence length histogram alert.
- Long-term actions: per-tenant memory quota gating (SRE ticket JIRA-2341), new canary for ingestion jobs (owner: Marco), and allocator tuning RFC (owner: Aisha).

4) Community lightning + RFC preview
- Aisha: preview of RFC - "per-tenant KV budgeting". Goal: allow product to set firm per-tenant KV caps to avoid noisy neighbors. Feedback requested: compatibility constraints with Private deployments.
- Request from Solutions Eng: better observability on cache hit-rates surfaced to CS dashboards; Lina to scope.

Q&A (recorded elects):
Q: Can quantization be enabled per-route to avoid code hallucination?
A: Yes — routing-by-policy will let us use route-level quantize flags; team to prototype and measure.

Q: Why did pre-warm increase cost?
A: Because we started pre-warming more nodes for shorter spikes; balancing act between latency SLO and cost. Owen to produce a per-pool cost vs latency graph next week.

Decisions made:
- Ship kv-cache LRU fix to 50% next week if canary telemetry remains stable. (Owner: Lina)
- Enable a per-route quantization flag pilot for two internal partners. (Owner: Marco)
- Keep autoscale pre-warm policy but gate it behind tenant-critical flag; SRE to add an opt-out. (Owner: Owen)

Action items (owner / due):
- Lina Chen: expand canary to 50% and run code-eval battery (due 2027-05-05).
- Marco Hernandez: land PR #7889 and add post-deploy cache integrity check (due 2027-05-03).
- Owen Park: produce cost-vs-latency graph for autoscale pre-warm policy + proposal for opt-out flag (due 2027-05-04).
- Aisha Patel: write RFC draft for per-tenant KV budgeting and circulate to eng + product (due 2027-05-07).
- SRE (assigned in JIRA-2341): implement per-tenant memory gating prototype (owner: Priya Kumar, due 2027-05-14).

Parking lot / Notes to self:
- Add a short demo of trace-tagged batches to next "Engineers' Café"; good educational piece for new hires.
- Follow up with Solutions Eng on CS dashboard pain points — make a short spike to prototype a 1-page view.
- Need a checklist for model-swap cache sanity checks in release playbook.

Recording + artifacts:
- Recording posted to #eng-serving-runtime channel (link in Confluence page).
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Engineers%27+Caf%C3%A9+Archive
- PR / issues: see linked_artifacts above.

Freeform notes (scratch):
- People liked the 2-min lightning spot — keep it.
- Consider rotating host to highlight different subteams.
- Slack thread: #eng-serving-runtime:thread-4k2h (lots of follow-up questions, see Marco's replies)

-- end of notes --
